title: QVAC shared test catalog
description:
The language-neutral shape of a test definition. A client in any language reads this to know which step operations exist, which fields each one requires, and which assertion names are legal — and can generate a stub per operation that fails loudly when it is not implemented, which is what turns `incomplete` from a reporting convention into something the code enforces.

NOT FROZEN. The vocabulary was read off the existing TypeScript executors and is expected to change while the first categories migrate. It freezes once two languages have run the same definitions across more than one category; the accompanying prose spec (docs/architecture/conforming-test-runner.md) says what a runner must DO with a legal definition, which a schema cannot express.

params.description: Parameters the test runs with; addressable from a step as $params.x

steps.description: Declarative test body. A definition without `steps` routes to its TypeScript executor unchanged, so migration is per-test and reversible.

suites.description: Suite tags. Beyond grouping, these say what a non-JS leg may leave out: engine-quality, packaging, imperative, host-idiomatic.

metadata.description: Repo-specific data: category, the resource key the test needs, estimated duration

retryOnFailure.description: Diagnostic reload retry. The test is reported failed regardless of the retry outcome.

ref.description: A literal, or a reference: $name for a value a previous step bound, $params.x for the test's own params. Paths may index, e.g. $result.blocks[0].text. A trailing ? marks the reference optional: a path that is not there resolves to nothing, and a call parameter that resolves to nothing is left off the call rather than passed as null

collect.description: How a streaming call is folded into a single value

expectation.description: What the asserted value is checked against. Shared data, so every client must read it identically.

oneOf.description: A JavaScript closure. Cannot cross the wire, so a non-JS client reports such a definition incomplete rather than failed. Being migrated to named assertions.

reason.description: Why. The reasons are the only record of why the matrix looks the way it does and must travel with the rule.

platforms.description: Skip only on these platforms, e.g. ["mobile-ios", "mobile-android"]

useModel.description: Load the models behind these resource keys. Everything not declared is evicted first, so a run does not depend on test order.

deps.description: Resource keys. A list, not a single key: some tests genuinely need two models at once.

modelSource.description: The model source behind a resource key, without loading it. A test that drives loadModel itself needs the source as data, and the source is the one thing a definition cannot write down: it is a per-client constant the resource table holds.

asset.description: Resolve a bundled test asset for this platform — a filesystem path on desktop, a bundled-asset URI on mobile.

call.description: One SDK call, through the client's public surface. A client that reached past it into the worker would prove only that the engine works.

callError.description: A call expected to fail; binds { code, message, hasCause }. `collect` folds the streaming result before deciding it failed, because a streaming call typically rejects only once its result is awaited

repeat.description: Run the nested steps once per item. Each iteration gets its own scope, so a binding cannot leak into the next.

project.description: Pull a field out of a bound value.

assert.description: Check a bound value. Either against the definition's own expectation, or with a shared named assertion.

with.description: Arguments for a named assertion; values may use $refs. Needed whenever a check compares the result against something the test set up — e.g. that the returned modelId is the one we just loaded.

compare.description: Compare two bound values with a shared named comparison.
